A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Scalable Sobolev IPM for Probability Measures on a Graph. The main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched reliably despite formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C.2 report original classification accuracy and computation-time experiments on four document datasets, Orbit, and MPEG7, including graph-size and slicing analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C.2 retain the original classification, computation-time, graph-size, and slicing results.

M1.justification: The critic constraint, weight function, closed-form computation, kernel construction, and sliced variant remain unchanged. The additional paragraph in Section 3.2 explains how to use existing precomputed quantities without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TWITTER, RECIPE, CLASSIC, AMAZON, Orbit, and the same 10-class MPEG7 subset using GLog and GSqrt graphs. The new graph illustration introduces no evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the OT, tree-Wasserstein, and Sobolev transport kernel comparators, including the same transport orders. Newly cited methods in v2 are discussed as related work rather than added to experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C.3 retain the same representations, 70%/30% training/test and validation splits, SVM strategy, hyperparameter grids, graph sizes, and timing procedure including preprocessing. No revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The analyses varying graph size, graph density, and number of slices are retained in Section 6 and Appendix C.2. Their plots are relocated and renumbered, with no added ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 repeats for training/test splits and hyperparameter validation, and retain the same plotted error bars. No new seed information, uncertainty procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: The experimental plots in v1 Figures 1–22 match v2 Figures 2–23, and Table 1 retains its values. The reported Orbit timing comparison remains over 39 hours for OT versus under 34 minutes for the regularized Sobolev IPM kernels.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs are retained. Appendix A.2 adds an equation number, and Appendix C.1 repairs an unresolved equation reference; neither changes the derivation. The added graph illustration and background discussion are explanatory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a fast closed-form regularization, metric equivalence and transport connections, positive-definite kernels, and preliminary classification benefits. The revised wording about comparing measures on a given graph makes explicit a scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly clarifies that the approach targets an equivalent, efficiently computable metric rather than tight error bounds or a sharp approximation to the original Sobolev IPM. It explicitly leaves those approximation questions for future investigation.

D1.justification: The introduction in v2 announces a code release and supplies a repository reference, which v1 lacks. Dataset-access instructions, hardware description, and experimental implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a focused distinction from Peyre (2018), contrasting the full Sobolev norm with a gradient-only seminorm. Additional citations and Appendix B.3 discussion cover tree-Wasserstein extensions, including Le and Nguyen (2021) and Tran et al. (2025a–d), without substantially changing the overall positioning.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain graph notation, the weight function, computation, and approximation scope. Author information and acknowledgements are updated, and a broken cross-reference is repaired. The section hierarchy and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of plots and the table. A new graph schematic becomes Figure 1, and the existing figures are renumbered and redistributed throughout the document.

improvement.justification: The code-access information, clearer computational explanation, and explicit approximation limits in Appendix C.3 modestly improve usability and conceptual clarity while preserving the theory and empirical evidence. These gains outweigh a limited new defect: Figure 1's caption incorrectly assigns shortest-path length two to every vertex pair despite its unit-length edges.
